sources.title: NASA Science — Dawn: Ion Propulsion
sources.read_scope: Body: Ion Propulsion System and Solar Power; browser lines 238-254, especially movable thrusters, one-at-a-time operation, xenon, low thrust, and gimbaled opposing solar arrays.
supports: Dawn has three movable ion thrusters operated one at a time.
Electrical power accelerates xenon ions; sustained low thrust differs from rapid launch acceleration.
Two opposing gimbaled photovoltaic wings provide spacecraft and thruster power.
limits: Dawn-specific dimensions, count, fuel, performance and layout do not define all ion spacecraft.
Internal ionization, exact thrust and accumulated delta-v cannot be proved by a still image.
A blue plume alone does not identify ion propulsion.

sources.title: NASA History — Deep Space 1 Validated the Promise of Ion Thrusters
sources.read_scope: Body and prototype-image caption; browser lines 258-267.
supports: A xenon ion-engine prototype was photographed through a vacuum-chamber port with faint blue emission.
Deep Space 1 demonstrated a solar-powered xenon electric-propulsion system.
limits: Caption concerns a laboratory prototype, not a universal in-flight exposure or plume appearance.
The page's spacecraft illustration and real test photograph must retain separate provenance labels.
Do not convert faint emission into a compulsory giant opaque blue exhaust flame.

sources.title: ESA — Thermal Control
sources.read_scope: Full short body; browser lines 9-26, including foil-like MLI and white or mirror-like radiators.
supports: Spacecraft thermal systems can include foil-like insulation blankets and white-painted or mirror-like radiators.
Radiators reject heat while multilayer insulation reduces incoming heating.
limits: Surface color alone cannot establish a panel's engineering function.
The source does not require every radiator to be white, wing-shaped, or visibly glowing.
A visible panel is not proof of adequate thermal capacity or internal coolant flow.

sources.title: NASA Science — Sail Along with NASA’s Solar Sail Tech Demo in Real-Time Simulation
sources.read_scope: Body lines 248-254: photon pressure, reflective sail, deployable composite booms; dated mission state is not adopted.
supports: Solar sailing uses sunlight pressure acting on a reflective sail.
The Advanced Composite Solar Sail System uses a deployable composite-boom system.
limits: The 2024 orbital and deployment status is historical context, not a newly verified current mission status.
A sail is not a photovoltaic power array or a fabric sail driven by atmospheric wind.
A single image cannot prove acceleration or force direction.

sources.title: NASA — Retrofuturistic NASA Space Art
sources.read_scope: Article and artwork caption; browser lines 243-259.
supports: Rick Guidice's doughnut-shaped space-colony illustration arose from NASA Ames's 1970s space-colony art/study context.
NASA explicitly labels the depicted colony fictional.
limits: Official hosting does not turn concept art into a photograph or a built habitat.
The caption alone does not specify every spoke, mirror, population, orbit, or rotation rate.
Retrofuturistic is an art-direction route; it must not silently impose a torus on all space-opera scenes.

sources.title: Harry W. Jones, NASA Ames — Long Term Human Presence in Space Requires Artificial Gravity and Radiation Shielding
sources.read_scope: Seven-page PDF opened; Section III, printed page 3 / PDF page 2, lines 105-144. Read wheel/torus, cylinder and tether concepts, radius/spin relation, and rotating/nonrotating-interface discussion. Page screenshot requested for the same section.
supports: Discusses torus/wheel, cylinder, and tether-with-balancing-mass approaches to rotating artificial-gravity habitats.
Names the O'Neill cylinder and Stanford torus as distinct large-habitat concepts.
Rotational acceleration depends on radius and angular speed; rotating and nonrotating interfaces create engineering complexity.
limits: Use as an authored technical paper, not NASA-wide consensus on every medical or settlement-policy assertion.
Do not adopt its categorical claim that rotation is the only possible gravity provision; thrust acceleration and fictional gravity systems are separate routes.
Standing people or ring geometry alone do not prove rotation, gravity level, shielding effectiveness, or habitability.
Detailed O'Neill land-strip/window layouts and Ringworld geometry require additional primary design sources.

sources.title: ESO — Panning across a Dyson sphere
sources.read_scope: Initial page open returned navigation but not the relevant body. Search returned the complete short description and credit; subsequent body opens timed out and an in-memory HTTP attempt returned 503. No video frames were inspected.
supports: The indexed ESO description calls the depiction a hypothetical thought experiment with solar-panel-like objects partially surrounding a star.
limits: Provisional lead only; re-open the body before using its geometry as adopted authoritative support.
No claim of visually reviewing the animation or its exact panel geometry.
The hypothetical illustration is not evidence that a Dyson structure has been discovered.

sources.title: Suazo et al. — Project Hephaistos I: Upper limits on partial Dyson spheres in the Milky Way
sources.read_scope: Opened 13-page primary-paper PDF and read page 1 introduction plus page 2 Section 2.1 models; browser lines 9-80 and 100-140. Read scope does not include the full empirical analysis or its figures.
supports: The introduction explicitly describes swarms of artificial light-absorbing components around stars as a hypothetical energy-harvesting structure.
The paper models optical obscuration and thermal waste heat; its covering factor is an intercepted fractional solid angle rather than a requirement for a rigid shell.
Its abstract distinguishes expected Dyson signatures from naturally occurring infrared interlopers.
limits: Does not provide a canonical panel size, rigid-shell architecture, habitable Ringworld surface or an observed Dyson object.
Infrared excess or a rendered glowing structure is not confirmation of alien engineering.
Do not report its 2022 numerical limits as the latest search result without a fresh literature review.

sources.title: NASA Astrobiology — Life, Here and Beyond / About Astrobiology
sources.read_scope: Body lines 32-50; migration notice at line 0 is retained as provenance context.
supports: Astrobiology studies life's origin, evolution and distribution; entertainment depictions of extraterrestrial beings are fiction rather than observed alien morphologies.
The page states that life beyond Earth had not been found.
limits: Migration-era overview; re-check the current NASA astrobiology site before using the no-discovery statement as a dated scientific-status headline.
Supplies no observed alien anatomy and cannot justify humanoid, insectoid, blue-skinned, silicon-based or hive-mind defaults.
This source supplies a scientific claim boundary, not a positive morphology template.

sources.title: NASA Science — What is a biosignature?
sources.read_scope: Learning-resource body: definitions and examples, lines 264-266, 336-340, 389-391.
supports: Biosignatures are evidence-bearing features or patterns for past or present life; candidate examples include layered microbial-mat mineral structures.
Technosignatures refer to possible evidence of technological life.
Earth remains the example used for known life and biological analogies.
limits: A rock pattern, molecule, atmosphere color, or instrument display does not independently prove life.
The source's educational examples are potential signs, not validated alien organisms.
Sentience, sapience, collective cognition, biological origin and technological capacity need separate evidence.

sources.title: Star Wars Databank — Imperial Star Destroyer
sources.read_scope: Official fiction entry body and dimensions, lines 26-50; related Republic cruiser description at lines 99-101.
supports: The Imperial Star Destroyer has a wedge-shaped capital-ship form, surface weapons and an underside hangar bay.
The entry gives a fictional length of 1,600 m and a hangar role supporting smaller craft.
limits: Star Wars canon/design evidence, not a universal scientific spacecraft specification.
Capital ship does not universally mean wedge silhouette, aircraft carrier, or a fixed size.
A nearby fighter does not prove hangar launch, ownership, fleet affiliation, or attack intent.

sources.title: Star Wars Databank — Death Star
sources.read_scope: Official entry body lines 29-31 and construction/weapon narrative lines 54-64; no video playback or independent image-shape review.
supports: The fictional Death Star is a moon-sized armed space station, distinct from an ordinary warship or natural moon.
The entry describes construction in space and a fictional planet-destroying capability.
limits: Moon-sized is an in-world scale claim; image framing alone does not establish its absolute diameter.
Do not promote a station's weapon capability, function, or destruction history to pixel-observable facts.
Generic battle stations need not copy this franchise's design or political meaning.

sources.title: Lucasfilm / StarWars.com — Star Wars Inside Intel: Hyperspace
sources.read_scope: Body lines 55-60, author role and fictional realspace/hyperspace distinction, blue-tunnel description, hyperdrive and navigation.
supports: Within Star Wars, hyperspace is a separate travel dimension and the blue swirling tunnel is an established visual depiction.
A hyperdrive and destination navigation are described as in-world mechanisms.
limits: Fictional mechanism, not verified faster-than-light physics.
A tunnel image cannot prove elapsed travel time, coordinate accuracy, speed, or dimensional transition.
Warp drive, wormhole, jump gate, star streaks and hyperspace are not interchangeable mechanisms or compulsory shared appearances.

sources.title: StarTrek.com — Forgotten Trek: Designing the Enterprise-C
sources.read_scope: Body lines 41-59, design lineage, saucer/engineering-hull/bridge/engine components, fabrication constraints and relative attachment distances.
supports: Enterprise-C design discussions distinguish saucer, engineering hull, impulse engines and warp nacelles.
Component proportions and attachment distances were deliberate model/design choices, with production constraints affecting the final form.
limits: Officially hosted retrospective quoting designers; not a general engineering paper or a universal Star Trek ship rule.
Nacelle geometry does not prove actual warp travel or power generation.
Generic exploration ships should not automatically inherit a franchise-specific saucer and paired-nacelle layout.

sources.title: NASA Science — Lagoon Nebula: Visible-light View vs. Infrared View
sources.read_scope: Body lines 302-315, dimensions/data lines 336-370, and Color Info lines 416-419.
supports: Gas/dust cavities, ridges and dark clumps change appearance across visible and near-infrared observations.
The released image combines filtered monochrome exposures assigned display hues.
The pictured region spans about four light-years; foreground vehicle scale and telescope-image scale are different layers.
limits: Do not call the assigned palette naked-eye natural color or literal gas coloration without the filter mapping.
The telescope image is not proof that a nearby pilot sees a bright dense cloud at the ship's local scale.
No image assets or video frames were downloaded or independently pixel-audited in this research task.

adoption_notes: This file proposes optional research cards, not CIDs, RIDs, runtime visual profiles or installed candidate-pack data.
Separate observed engineering, speculative engineering, official fictional convention, authored interpretation and telescope display mapping in source/provenance fields.

T07 remains a search excerpt. T08 was subsequently opened as a full primary PDF and its introduction/model section supports the swarm topology; exact panel styling, rigid-shell and inhabited-ring engineering remain separate follow-ups.
Before adoption compare existing concept units, owner bindings, affected dimensions and conditions, then choose reuse/refine/new/context/defer per component.
Do not bundle torus, battle fleet, blue plume, humanoid alien and multicolor nebula as mandatory consequences of the broad space-opera label.
Still-image gates use visible/partial/unobservable with partial_is_fail and UNOBSERVABLE_NOT_PASS. Source validity, retrieval success, generated pixels and requester acceptance remain separate.
For each retained card test a positive scene, a nearest-confusion negative, wrong-owner negative, occluded-endpoint case and underdetermined-mechanism case in both Korean and English.

High-priority remaining primary-source gaps: full Ringworld stellar-ring design; detailed O'Neill surface/mirror layout; fusion/antimatter propulsion architecture; thrust gravity; ECLSS component paths; orbital elevator endpoints/tether; light-lag and ansible mechanism boundaries; fictional shield/tractor-beam visual conventions; symbiosis/parasitism versus mere attachment.
